final.executive_summary: Hold AAPL and do nothing at the next open: keep_shares, target_weight_now = null, retaining the existing 6.4149 shares (~$1,991, 2.0% of $99,894 total equity) with cash unchanged at ~$97,904. All three risk seats independently converged on 2.0% keep_shares and both the Research Manager and Trader proposed the same, so the conflict in this round is about framing (the aggressive analyst calls 2% a 'fee-efficient call option'; the conservative correctly notes holding is not free after $27.92 of cumulative fees and -$111 realized) rather than about direction or size. At 310.34, both available transactions are struck at their worst price: adding sits beneath five supply layers at 0.94:1 near-term reward-to-risk with MACD -1.488 below its -1.253 signal and volume at 34.7M versus a 55M confirmation threshold, while liquidating sells at a four-times-tested 300.00-302.94 floor that has never closed below with a rising 200-SMA at 281.70 to save only ~0.18% of total equity. Higher 4.0-5.0% and lower 0% are both rejected; scale to 4-5% only on a daily close above 316.83 on >55M shares with a MACD crossover, and cut to 0-1% only on a daily close below 300.57 on >60M shares. Horizon 1-3 months, re-underwritten at the late-October FQ4 FY2026 print.
final.investment_thesis:
The rating is Hold because the evidence is genuinely balanced after weighing, not because the analysts disagreed. All three risk seats landed on 2.0% / keep_shares, and I weigh their merits independently of speaking order: the aggressive analyst wins the direction (a four-times-tested 300.00-302.94 floor at 08-03, 08-04, 08-12, 08-17 that has never closed below, price +10.17% above a rising 200-SMA at 281.70, EPS +22.4% on revenue +16.1%, $62.22B net cash with $14.38B gross debt retired and no new long-term paper, $117.0B nine-month CFO, receivables -21.1% against revenue +16.1% so earnings are not buyback-manufactured), the conservative and neutral analysts win the expression (no transaction is fee-free and both candidate transactions carry negative near-term expectancy).

Where the bear genuinely wins and it governs sizing: the bull's own reward-to-risk construction fails arithmetic. A 310.34 entry against a 300.00 floor stop risks $10.34 to a first target of 320.04, a reward of $9.70, i.e. 0.94:1; the add-above-316.83 leg to 333.43 is $16.83 of risk against $16.60 of reward, ~0.99:1. The bull's '2:1' exists only if you buy the bottom of the zone and exit at the full gap fill through five separate supply layers (313.36 / 316.83-319.28 / the 320.28 50% retrace rejection / 324.77 / 329.59-333.43, the last including the 132.5M shares distributed on 07-31). MACD at -1.488 sits below its -1.253 signal and below zero since 08-11, price is under the 50-SMA at 310.50 and the 313.01 Bollinger mid, volume has fallen to 34.7M (roughly a quarter of the shock day) against a 55M confirmation threshold, and ATR has compressed to 7.37 (-25%) into a known volatility event with NVDA earnings and Jackson Hole in the same week. The aggressive analyst's claim of a 'mild positive divergence' at the 08-12 low is not in the supplied technical evidence, which explicitly declined to claim a clean one; and the +8.8% deferred revenue against +16.1% revenue growth is deferred revenue growing at half the top-line rate, a mild negative mix tell for the Services margin story, not a bullish backlog. The margin-fragility arithmetic is the strongest fundamental point in the round and is unresolved: revenue +16.1%, COGS +11.2%, opex +21.9%, R&D +32.5% at 9.34% of revenue, so all FY2026 operating-margin expansion is gross margin doing 100% of the work while the cost line outgrows the top line, and the news pack's own 1-2 quarter pass-through lag puts the exposure quarters in Q4 FY26 / Q1 FY27, unobservable today with no company guidance anywhere in the evidence set.

Where the bull genuinely wins and why this is not Sell or Underweight: the bear's core case is explicitly multiple compression - 'a de-rating requires nothing to go wrong fundamentally' - which names no catalyst, no date and no mechanism, and a 16% de-rating can take two quarters or two years. The bear himself concedes the business is sound and advises trimming into 316.83-320.28, not into 310.34. Selling at 310.34 means selling at the bottom of a 17-session base (range midpoint 310.14) with price pinned inside a $1.35 convergence band where the 50-SMA (310.50), 10-EMA (310.35), VWMA (309.15) and the 07-31 gap bottom (310.69) all meet. That monetizes the bear's weakest entry point; adding monetizes the bull's weakest entry point with a negative-expectancy first leg. Neither is justified.

Total exposure and the higher/lower comparison. Retained total exposure is 2.0% of total account equity (~$1,991), inside an approved 0-5% band. The concrete higher alternative is 4.0-5.0% (~$4,000-5,000, roughly 6.5 added shares, ~$2 in fees): it would capture ~+0.33-0.37% of total equity on a full gap fill to 329.59-333.43 versus ~+0.13-0.15% at 2%, but it doubles downside exposure directly beneath five rejection layers with a contracting ATR ahead of an event week and a confirmed-negative MACD - sizing up in anticipation rather than on confirmation is how a good thesis becomes a bad trade. The concrete lower alternative is 0% (sell all 6.4149 shares, ~$1,991, ~$2 in fees): it is defensible on the still-unexplained 07-31 -7.35% / 132.5M-share gap alone, but it forgoes all participation in a business compounding EPS at 22% with $62B of net cash and a rising 200-SMA, at a price that already embeds the bear's ~$8.83 deceleration case (~35x on ~$8.75 TTM), and it saves at most ~0.18% of total equity on the 200-SMA (-9.2%) scenario or ~0.07% on a break of 300 (-3.3%). Cash opportunity cost is real and is weighed, not dismissed: with ~98% of the account in non-interest-bearing cash, a full gap fill to 329.59-333.43 forgoes roughly 0.15-0.35% of equity depending on size, but that is not enough to justify pre-positioning ahead of unquantified margin risk with no confirmed volume, and cash opportunity cost does not automatically override the downside case any more than risk avoidance overrides it.

Tiny-position justification, stated as economics rather than as 'observation.' Observing evidence requires no stock, so 2.0% is not justified as an observation position; it is a deliberately capped participation stake whose purpose is to hold a real, fee-efficient claim on range resolution higher (+6.2-7.5% to 329.59-333.43, worth ~+0.13-0.15% of the account) without pre-committing capital to a thesis whose margin engine is single-variable and whose next two data points (Q4 FY26 gross margin and whether the +$13.27B gross intangibles step-up is disclosed) are unavailable. Its account-level contribution is intentionally marginal in both directions, ~±0.15-0.2% of total equity. It is preferable to zero because holding a toe-hold at a four-times-tested floor is materially cheaper than re-establishing one from scratch after a volume-confirmed breakout, and it is preferable to 4-5% because the near-term reward-to-risk is below 1:1. The account already trimmed to 2.0% on 08-24 (~$1.00 in fees); the conservative analyst is right that holding is not free - cumulative trading fees are $27.92 with -$111.00 realized - but that argues against another marginal trade, not for a different size. A further proportional trim to ~1% would change account-level risk by ~0.1% while paying fees and would signal action without new evidence; the 08-17 AAPL lesson (an Underweight at a triple-tested support with a live golden cross and price above a rising 200-SMA lost +2.7% alpha in five days) is directly on point: require a confirmed break before expressing a tape view at support. Conversely the 08-14 lesson - pre-commit size at the floor when the risk is bounded by arithmetic - is bounded here by the sub-1:1 first-leg ratio, so it argues for preserving the existing stake, not enlarging it, until confirmation prints.

Disagreement resolved. Aggressive vs conservative on framing: I adopt the conservative/neutral framing that 2% is a neutral participation right rather than positive expectancy, but that framing does not change the action because the marginal transaction - in either direction - is negative-expectancy at 310.34. All three seats agree on 2.0% and keep_shares, and I authorize that without a dissenting size. The MFI scale anomaly was discarded and the 08-17 to 08-21 news gap, the 85 of 105 un-supplied news records, the absence of insider or sentiment data, the unexplained 07-31 gap, the $13.27B gross intangibles increase with zero new long-term debt and no 8-K, and the unresolved 08-22 CEO-succession headline are stated as gaps, not papered over; because they cut in both directions they support capping exposure rather than expanding or eliminating it.

What would change it: a daily close above 316.83 on >55M shares with a MACD crossover flips the VWMA 309.15 cost basis from resistance to support and justifies scaling toward 4-5%; a daily close below 300.57 on >60M shares (below 300.00 preferable) breaks the only tested floor in the dataset and justifies cutting to 0-1%, with 290.88 and then the 200-SMA at 281.70 as references. Between those triggers, do nothing - at a 2.0% cap no single AAPL outcome moves total equity by more than ~0.2%, so daily rebalancing around this position is unjustified.
